html:
Magtymguly Pyragy was a Turkmen poet and Sufi thinker of the 18th century, born in about 1724 in the Atrek valley on the edge of Persia, and the national poet of the Turkmen.

He studied in madrasas in Khiva and Bukhara. He wrote in Turkmen rather than Persian, in plain verse that ordinary herders could learn by heart. His poems mourn the wars between the Turkmen tribes and the raids of Persian armies, and call on the tribes to unite as one people with one land, an idea far ahead of its time.

His poems were passed on mostly by singers. In the Soviet and independent eras he became the symbol of Turkmen nationhood, with statues, a city and a university named after him. In Turkmenistan his verse is learned in school alongside the national story, after the fall of Geok Tepe ended Turkmen freedom.
